# Homework 03B — Cleaning Messy Data

### How to turn it in

Run your code in an R script and paste your **code and output** into a Word document to submit. For every task, briefly explain *what was wrong* before you show the fix — a line of code with no explanation is not enough.

::: callout-tip
## Loading the data

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

leaf_raw_df <- read_csv("data/messy_leaf_data.csv")
```

Do not pass `na = c(...)` on this first read — Task 1 asks you to discover the missing-value codes yourself.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Task 1 — Detect the mess (2 pts)

Using `glimpse()` and `count()`, find and list: (a) the column with the wrong data type, (b) every disguised missing-value code you can find in `weight_g`, and (c) every distinct spelling of a category in `side`.

### Task 2 — Fix the text (2 pts)

Fix the `side` column so it has exactly two clean categories. Show `count(side)` before and after your fix.

### Task 3 — Fix the missing values (2 pts)

Reload the file, correctly telling `read_csv()` about every missing-value code you found in Task 1. Confirm with `count(is.na(weight_g))` that the count of missing values now matches what you expected.

### Task 4 — Rescue the numeric column (2 pts)

Use `parse_number()` to fix whichever column was stored as text because of a units-contaminated entry. Confirm with `glimpse()` that it is now `<dbl>`.

### Task 5 — Duplicates and outliers (2 pts)

Find and remove any exact duplicate row using `duplicated()` and `distinct()`. Then flag (do not delete) any `weight_g` value above 20 g. For the flagged row, write one sentence on what you think the real value probably was and why you are not simply changing it yourself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Task 6 — Reflection (bonus, 1 pt)

In 2–3 sentences: why is it dangerous to run `mean(weight_g, na.rm = TRUE)` on this dataset *before* doing any of the cleaning above? Be specific about which uncleaned value would distort the mean the most.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Grading notes *(instructor — remove before posting)*

11 pts total (10 + 1 bonus). T1 detection (2) · T2 text fix + before/after counts (2) · T3 correct `na = c(...)` set (2) · T4 `parse_number()` + type check (2) · T5 duplicate removal + outlier flag with reasoning (2) · T6 bonus reflection (1). Common struggle points: students forget `height_cm` uses a *different* missing code than `weight_g`, and are tempted to silently overwrite the flagged outlier rather than leaving it flagged.

*End of Homework 03B.*
